U.S. Department of Energy (2014). Improving Motor and Drive System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry. Advanced Manufacturing Office, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy; prepared by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Resource Dynamics Corporation and Washington State University Energy Program; produced by NREL with support from the Copper Development Association. DOE/GO-102014-4356, February 2014.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 10). A guidance sourcebook (system basics, maintenance, VFD application, economics, resources); it holds almost no technology-level numbers: no savings ranges per pump/fan/compressed-air system, no VFD efficiencies and no costs. Main file: the only technology number, AC induction motor full-load efficiency 85-97%. Other statements (synchronous +1-2 points, LCC 96/3/1%, loss shares) in _other-values. Appendix B repeats the NEMA EE/Premium minimum tables also in McCoy and Douglass 2014 (mccoy_2014_001); not extracted. The system-level savings the task hoped for are in the separate AMO pumping, fan and compressed-air sourcebooks, not this one.
